conditions.text: All four events came from app version 3.1.0 on iOS 18.4, device iPhone15,2, so set up that combination to match the observed environment.
Push was deliverable in every event: OS permission ALLOWED and provider registration REGISTERED; the profile was also consistent in every event.

Every step and precondition in the packet has support 1.0 across the 4 events considered, so the packet does not identify any condition that varies or is optional; whether the push and profile states are actually required to trigger the crash is not established by the packet.
To reproduce reliably you will likely need the applications endpoint to fail with a 500, since that response is present in all observed events.
Commit c31a111 ("MEI-40: Apply to jobs from the detail page") touches the same file as the culprit frame, src/modules/jobs/detail.vue, making it a lead worth checking rather than a confirmed cause.

missing_evidence_questions.text: What object is undefined at src/modules/jobs/detail.vue:31 when 'jobId' is read, and where was it expected to be set?
What causes POST /api/applications to return 500, and does the crash still occur when that call succeeds?
Is the crash specific to app 3.1.0 / iOS 18.4 / iPhone15,2, or do other versions and devices reproduce it? The packet only contains events from this one combination.
Do the push and profile states matter at all, or are they incidental to these 4 events?
Did commit c31a111 introduce the code path at line 31, and does the crash predate it?
Does the specific job selected from li.job-card affect whether the failure occurs?

steps_prose.text: Tap a job card (li.job-card) in the list.
The backend call POST /api/applications returns 500, and onApplyClick at src/modules/jobs/detail.vue:31 throws the TypeError while reading 'jobId' off an undefined value.

summary.text: Four Sentry events show a TypeError "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'jobId')" thrown in onApplyClick at src/modules/jobs/detail.vue line 31, occurring when a user taps Apply on a job detail page and the POST /api/applications call returns 500.
